about: Prioritised inventory of resident and business processes for Charlottesville (independent city), Albemarle County and Staunton (independent city), Virginia. It deduplicates the three discovery files within each locality, aligns the same process across localities under one process id, adds state-backbone processes where a locality's court page was read, ranks every process, and selects up to 20 per locality to model next.
built_by: Claude (claude-opus-5-5), from the files listed in inputs; read-only
status: design fixture; nothing here is loaded into the DB, the wiki or Wikibase
inputs: curated/places/va/charlottesville.json (to skip the records and business processes it already answers)

method.dedup: Within a locality, discovery entries that answer the same resident question were merged under one process id; merged_from lists the discovery ids, and the first one (or the one named in the build's primary list) supplies the office. Examples: new and renewal business licences; paying real estate and personal property tax; assessor review and Board of Equalization appeal; starting and stopping utility service; pay, waiver and appeal of a parking ticket; residential, trade permits and inspection scheduling.
method.alignment: The same process carries the same id in every locality (for example bpol_business_license, building_permit_residential, real_estate_tax_relief_elderly_disabled, public_records_request, voter_registration, marriage_license, dog_license, zoning_variance, short_term_rental_registration). process_ids lists every id with the localities that have it.
method.state_backbone: For each process that is the main subject of a state-backbone topic, the topic's Code sections are added to legal_hints, its locality office page (where read) to sources, and its locality observations to backbone_observed. Processes with no discovery entry were added only where the backbone records an official office page that was read (court pages on vacourts.gov); they carry basis 'state_backbone'.
method.priority: high: needed often by many residents or businesses and governed by rules or deadlines with legal consequences, or legally consequential with deadlines for a common group. medium: regular but narrower, or frequent but low-stakes (account changes, purchases, reports). low: rare, or a service booking, sign-up, lookup or program with little procedure. Frequent self-service lookups, sign-ups and bookings are capped at medium or low because there is little procedure to model. Processes run by a separate or regional body (school division, library, service or solid waste authority, regional social services, VDOT) are ranked for the locality's own role.
method.selection: Up to 20 per locality: every high process, then medium processes in one shared order of importance, preferring a clear legal basis (a state-backbone topic) and an official procedure page, so that the same processes are modelled in all three places. Charlottesville's public_records_request and bpol_business_license are not selected because curated/places/va/charlottesville.json already answers them (records, business).
method.frequency: frequency.level is normalised to very_common, common, occasional, rare. Staunton's scale maps very_high to very_common, high to common, medium to occasional, low and rare to rare; source_level keeps the original. All levels are estimates from the discovery files, not local statistics.
method.detail: Selected processes carry full detail: every office channel, forms, all evidence quotes, backbone observations and caveats. Unselected processes keep the index fields (office name and page, frequency level, priority, sources, legal hints); their forms, quotes and notes stay in the discovery file under the ids in merged_from.
method.quotes: Every quote is copied programmatically from the discovery file or state-backbone.json that recorded it, with its source. In this pass: state-law quotes of selected processes were checked against the lexflow Virginia index text; Charlottesville page quotes were re-fetched from the live city pages; Albemarle page quotes were re-checked on the Internet Archive copies the discovery file read; Staunton page quotes were not re-checked (see the locality's access note). Each selected quote's 'checked' field says which.
method.privacy: Offices and official channels only: office names, office pages, main lines, office addresses and role mailboxes as recorded on the office's own page by the discovery files. A mailbox named after an office-holder title (manager, mayor, director) is dropped. No staff names or personal mailboxes.

verification.manual_checks: Five quotes failed the automatic substring check only because of spacing at HTML tag boundaries (for example 'March 1st .'); each was compared by hand with the fetched page text and matches word for word.
verification.fetch_rules: Live and archive pages were fetched with User-Agent 'lexflow-research/0.1 (https://github.com/alibama/lexflow)', after reading robots.txt, at least 1.5 seconds apart (4 seconds for the archive retry). Nothing was submitted and no one was contacted.

va:albemarle.access: www.albemarle.org refuses automated requests (HTTP 403, robots.txt included). The discovery file read official pages from Internet Archive copies (each quote's read_via). In this pass every page quote of the selected processes was re-checked against those archive copies on 2026-10-10 and found word for word.
gaps: Small claims, traffic tickets and name changes were not in the discovery file; they are added from the state backbone (Albemarle General District and Circuit Court pages on vacourts.gov).

Candidates the discovery file lists as not yet researched: agricultural-forestal districts and the ACE conservation easement program, Economic Development Authority incentives, VDH well and septic permits and VDOT entrance permits, the district courts' own processes, school meals, transportation and records (ACPS), and the Town of Scottsville's services.

Some county pages could not be read even from the archive (burn permit, SNAP, tax relief and home occupation How Do I pages, the floodplain, VESCP, VSMP and water and sewer application pages); their processes keep the URLs from the site menu.
notes: Form of government: the discovery file confirms from the county's own page that Albemarle uses the county executive form, so the Department of Finance & Budget holds the commissioner of the revenue and treasurer powers (Va. Code §§ 15.2-521, 15.2-522). The state backbone had assumed this without reading the county site.
The county's website terms forbid redistributing or reposting site content without written permission; quotes are kept to one short sentence for citation (discovery file, website_terms).

Albemarle has no elected Treasurer; collection is done by the Department of Finance & Budget under the county executive form (Va. Code §§ 15.2-519, 15.2-522).
